canonical_topic: Major crude oil benchmarks: WTI, Brent, Persian Gulf
definition: WTI and Brent are the two liquid, tradable crude oil benchmark contracts; Persian Gulf crude is a third common reference but has no comparably liquid futures contract, only spot prices from Oman and Dubai.
core_idea: The industry references crude quality and price mainly through a small set of benchmarks, of which only WTI (U.S. production) and Brent (North Atlantic seaborne delivery) have active liquid contract markets.
key_points: WTI: benchmark for crude produced in the United States.
Brent: benchmark for crude delivered by ship in the northern Atlantic.
Persian Gulf crude: referenced via Oman and Dubai spot prices, no equivalent liquid futures contract.
WTI and Brent are both classified as light, sweet ("premium") crude oils.
trading_implications: Liquidity differences mean WTI/Brent serve as tradable price references while Persian Gulf crude pricing relies on spot assessments rather than futures hedging.
